title: etbb-july-2024-february-2026-update.pdf — section 190
text:
62. The person involved should be addressed directly and in a usual manner, unless it is clear
that some other approach should be adopted. Judges should face this person if possible –
with lip-reading this is particularly important.

63. Focus on the individual rather than on any impairment. This can be done by asking what is
needed rather than asking about the nature and extent of the impairment, eg “Do you need
assistance to read this?” rather than “Is your sight impaired?”

64. If the condition is known, or disclosed, remember that within any condition there may be
varying levels of impairment, so a general knowledge of the condition and its effects may
be inadequate to deal with the particular individual appropriately, although it is a start.

65. People vary in their sensitivity about disclosing their disability, so any questioning needs
to be sensitive. Where a condition may require regular breaks, eg to rest or use the lavatory,
agree how the disabled person can indicate the need for a break that minimises any
embarrassment the person may feel when asking.
